title: VPC afterburner: automated API priming, model warmup and sanity checks after private deployment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: implement a robust, automated post-deploy validation runbook ("afterburner") for Private/VPC deployments that verifies API readiness, performs model load tests, and executes a suite of smoke/inference checks.

Scope: any private deployment created by the Terraform IaC modules. The automation must be network-local (run inside the customer VPC or via a temporary probe instance), not dependent on hosted control-plane-only services.

Why: recent incidents during private upgrades showed undetected model serving regressions (slow cold model load, KV cache misses, occasional OOM on large-ctx models) until customer workloads hit them. Early detection prevents customer impact and shortens rollbacks.

Acceptance approach: after Terraform apply finishes, trigger a deterministically repeatable validation run that: (1) confirms API health and auth (healthz, /v1/models list, token auth), (2) loads configured model binaries and measures model load time and memory, (3) runs a small suite of inference smoke tests across 3 representative models, (4) verifies KV cache warmup behavior and cache hit-rate patterns, (5) performs a short synthetic concurrency trial to validate autoscaling policies. Results are uploaded to a dashboard and must meet thresholds to mark deployment Ready.

Automation design decisions:
- Runner placement: use an ephemeral 'probe-runner' EC2/GCE instance created inside the same VPC via Terraform module outputs (preferred) OR a container executed by the customer-side bastion if customers opt-out of temporary instances.
- Trigger mechanism: Terraform post-apply hook writes the probe-runner bootstrap script to S3; a short-lived GitHub Actions job can also be used for CI-driven private deployments.
- Implementation language: Go or Python; we prototyped in Python for faster iteration (see GH PR).
- Failures: non-blocking versus blocking decision is configurable per project. By default, the afterburner will FAIL the pipeline for P1 regressions (model load > threshold, critical auth failures) and WARN for low-confidence metrics (minor latency regressions).

Key metrics & thresholds (initial):
- API readiness: /healthz returns 200 within 15s of instance becoming reachable.
- Model load: full model+KV load completes in <= 120s for base LLM-13B; <= 60s for LLM-7B.
- First-token latency (cold): p95 <= 500ms for small models (<=7B) and <= 1200ms for 13B on dedicated hardware profiles.
- KV cache warmup: cache hit-rate reaches >= 60% for repeated prefix requests after synthetic priming sequence of 50 tokens.
- Memory safety: resident memory growth stays within expected profile (no >10% unexpected spike).

Artifacts & integration points:
- Terraform module: private-deploy/modules/probe-runner (PR linked below).
- CI job: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/actions/afterburner.yaml
- Dashboard: Grafana panel (https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/vrVPC/afterburner-results)
- Runbook: Confluence - Private Deploy Afterburner Playbook (link below).

Rollout plan: land probe-runner module and a minimal afterburner script in canary first (internal staging regions). Run across 10 recent private clusters to validate thresholds and iterate. Once metrics stable, enable by default in next private deploy template and include opt-out flag.
acceptance_criteria: 1) After Terraform apply, an automated run completes and uploads results; 2) Health endpoints verified; 3) Representative models load within thresholds; 4) Smoke inference passes on 3 model families; 5) Dashboard shows run artifacts and pass/fail status; 6) Documentation and runbook published; 7) Two staging runs without false positives.
comments: 2026-02-25 — Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after post-upgrade incident analysis. Proposed 'probe-runner' approach to keep tests network-local and reduce external dependencies.

2026-03-01 — Marco Ruiz: Prototype script (python) validated basic health checks on staging. Observed model load for 13B at ~135s on staging infra; planned follow-up to tune serialization options and kernel selection.
2026-03-03 — Emily Chen (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Requested that auth token rotation and expiring creds be tested; added additional check to validate signed requests and KMS-backed key access.
2026-03-05 — Marco Ruiz: GH PR opened (private-deploy#198). CI job definition added. Noted intermittent KV cache misses during concurrent priming; hypothesize race in KV cache population path.

2026-03-07 — Priya Singh (PM): Approved thresholds for initial rollout but requested logging of raw perf traces for first 50 canary runs. Also requested a 'soft-fail' mode for enterprise customers until we complete 2 weeks of canary telemetry.
2026-03-09 — Marco Ruiz: Added sequential priming step to prototype to avoid simultaneous large model memory pressure. Staging runs now complete without OOMs. Preparing long soak runs this week.
2026-03-10 — Liam O'Connor (Security): Quick review done. Confirmed no secrets leaked to external CI logs; recommended tightening Probe-runner IAM role and least-privilege S3 access.
